subject: Aligning on buying criteria & deployment options
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena.rivas@healthsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Aligning on buying criteria & deployment options

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can shape the mutual action plan: 

1) Decision criteria you listed:
   - Latency target: 95th percentile <= 120ms for in-app routing (mobile clients)
   - Unit cost target: <= $0.003 per generated token for peak steady-state
   - Data residency: US-only production data
   - Deployment preference: evaluating Dedicated vs Private (you said security will weigh heavily)

2) Next steps we proposed:
   - Technical benchmark: run a short latency/cost profile on a sample prompt set (we'll need a 25–50 prompt seed from you)
   - Procurement intro: connect procurement/legal to go over standard terms + any SOC2 evidence requests
   - Economics: provide a high-level committed vs pay-as-you-go cost comparison for Dedicated vs Hosted

Questions from our side to confirm before we set calendars:
- Who is the economic buyer for AI platform + committed capacity (name/title)?
- Which team will own the procurement packet (procurement@healthsync.com or internal SSO contact)?
- Security asks: do you need an on-site review or will the SOC2 report + standard KMS integration detail suffice?

I attached a short CSV with the latency scenarios we typically test and a stubbed security QA workbook (HealthSync_Security_QA.xlsx) to start capturing items for your team. 

Proposed times for a 45m follow-up: Thu 11/5 10:00–10:45 PT or Mon 11/9 09:00–09:45 PT. Reply with the best slot and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: latency_targets_v1.csv (CSV), HealthSync_Security_QA.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Elena Rivas <elena.rivas@healthsync.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning on buying criteria & deployment options

Thanks Ava — good summary and appreciate the attachments. A few clarifications: 

- Economic buyer: That will be Priya Malhotra, VP Platform (cc'ing Priya on the next thread internally).
- Procurement: procurement@healthsync.com owns the contract flow; they will need draft terms and standard SLAs.
- Security: SOC2 + KMS details are a good start. We may request an architecture walkthrough (recorded session) but not an on-site review unless something specific comes up.

Latency: 120ms p95 is right for user-facing product. If you can show an expected p99 under a typical burst profile that would help the reliability conversation.

We can do Thu 11/5 10:00 PT. I'll ask procurement to join and will confirm the economic buyer before the call.

Elena
Director of Product
HealthSync
elena.rivas@healthsync.com

Adding a couple of notes from an internal procurement/ops perspective so HealthSync has visibility before Thu: 

- For Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity): typical procurement asks we see — monthly committed spend + a 6–12 month term. If Priya is the econ buyer, we'll prepare a committed pricing sheet showing TCO vs hosted.
- SLA: Our enterprise SLA shows 99.9% uptime and differentiated latency tiers (we can offer an SLA-backed p95 latency SLO for an agreed model family and region). We will call out exception handling and automated fallback to a compatible model family if pods are unhealthy.
- Security evidence: we can provide SOC2 type II report, encryption at rest/in transit docs, and a KMS integration summary. If they require an HSM diagram or specific key lifecycle details, Marcus can provide a short note.

Marcus — can you attach the KMS integration quicksheet and a sample SLA paragraph we can share on Thu?

Ava/Elena — for the benchmark we can run an initial 1k-token generator profile on a weighted prompt set (ava: we'll need the seed prompts). We’ll include p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens in the results.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Elena and team. Confirming the plan for Thu 11/5 10:00–10:45 PT:

Agenda (45m):
- 5m introductions (Priya / procurement)
- 10m technical benchmark plan + sample prompts (we'll capture any additional test cases)
- 10m SLA/ops & deployment modes (Dedicated vs Private economics)
- 10m security evidence review (SOC2, KMS summary)
- 10m open Q&A & next steps (mutual action plan + timeline)

Action items before the call:
- Elena: confirm Priya (econ buyer) will join and share any procurement paperwork we should review ahead of time.
- HealthSync procurement: if there are minimum required contract clauses or an internal PO process, please send a short note to procurement@redwoodinference.com.
- Elena: please share the 25–50 prompt seed set and a couple of high-sensitivity examples if you have them (we will treat those as PII-sensitive test data).
- Marcus: attaching KMS_quicksheet_v1.pdf and sample_SLA_paragraph.docx (see attached to this thread).

If anything changes on timing, I can move the invite — otherwise I’ll send the calendar invite now with a short Zoom link. Looking forward to closing the procurement window quickly so we can schedule the benchmarking run.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
